transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because my in-laws moved into our house, and since then I’ve been constantly keyed up and worn down. I’m snapping at my wife, avoiding calls I’d normally handle right away, and I almost let a musician’s contract fall apart because I just couldn’t think straight.
Do you feel these problems started because your in-laws moved into your house?

Yes. Things really changed after they moved in. I’ve been constantly on edge and exhausted, snapping at my wife, putting off calls I’d normally deal with right away. I nearly let a musician’s contract fall apart because I just couldn’t think clearly.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?
I’m not sure I’d call it depressed. I’ve mostly just been wound up and drained by everything.
If your in-laws moved out and the situation at home settled down, do you think these symptoms would mostly go away?
I think so, but they’re still living with us, so I haven’t really had a chance to see. The situation hasn’t settled down yet.
Aside from the situation with your in-laws, have you been worrying a lot about many other parts of your life?
I’m not sure. I mean, most of what’s been on my mind lately seems tied to what’s going on at home.
How long have you been feeling this keyed up and worn down since your in-laws moved in?
About a month now—basically since my in-laws moved into our home.
Has this stress been interfering with your work?

Yes. I nearly lost a musician’s contract because I wasn’t handling things the way I normally would, and my managing partner has questioned whether I can still be trusted with major negotiations. It’s been bad at home too—my wife pushed for us to get outside help because the conflict got so serious.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about many different parts of your life, not just the situation with your in-laws?
I don’t think it’s many different things. It keeps coming back to the situation at home and the fallout from that.
Have you been losing interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid much attention to that specifically.
Have you been feeling sad or down most days?
I’m not sure I’d say sad most days. I’ve been preoccupied and stressed about everything going on, but I haven’t really stopped to label it as feeling down.
Have you been feeling sad or hopeless?
I’m not sure. I wouldn’t say I’ve felt hopeless exactly. I’ve mostly been caught up in the stress of the situation.
During this past month, have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?
I honestly haven’t noticed a clear loss of interest. I’ve been so focused on everything else that I haven’t really paid attention to whether I’m enjoying things less.
Over the past month, have you felt sad most days?
I don’t think so. I’ve been under a lot of stress, but I haven’t really felt sad on most days.
During the past month, have you felt hopeless?
I wouldn’t say hopeless, no. I’ve felt overwhelmed by it all, but not like there’s no point or no way forward.
Have you been crying more than usual?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed myself crying more than usual.
During the past month, have you been feeling worthless?
I’m not sure I’d call it worthless. I’ve been stressed and hard on myself at times, but I haven’t really felt like I have no value.
Before your in-laws moved in, had you already been feeling anxious or worrying a lot on most days for at least 6 months?
I’m not sure. I can’t really say whether it was most days for that long.
Before your in-laws moved in, were you already worrying excessively on most days?
No. I was functioning normally before they moved in. The worrying didn’t start until a few weeks after they took over the house.
Since your in-laws moved in, have you been feeling depressed?
I wouldn’t say depressed exactly. I’ve been really worn down and on edge since they moved in, and it’s affecting everything.
Since your in-laws moved in, have you felt sad or depressed at all?
I’m not really sure I’d call it sadness or depression. It’s more that I feel worn down by the whole situation.
